e2eBuildCacheFinding.verdict: PRIMARY finding of the week, and it REPLACES the mechanism pass 1 proposed. The e2e 'Build' step is bimodal, and the mode is set by whether the Next.js build cache restored anything — not by time of day.
evidence: All 8 of the 11-16 runs started 06:50Z-08:22Z, i.e. all in pass 1's 'fast' <17:00Z bucket, yet e2e Build ranged 26s..110s.
Per-run, e2e 'Cache Next.js builds' restore seconds vs e2e 'Build' seconds: 1s->89, 1s->110, 1s->103, 2s->99, 1s->86, 1s->104, 4s->28, 3s->26.
That separates perfectly on 8/8 runs: restore <=2s => Build 86-110s (median ~101); restore >=3s => Build 26-28s. A 1s restore means nothing was restored at all.

'Post Cache Next.js builds' took 10-15s on ALL 8 runs, including the two fast ones, so the exact primary key missed every time and a new entry was written every time. The two fast runs were rescued by a restore-keys fallback that was still warm.
e2e 'Run e2e tests' was 43-51s on all 8 runs regardless of Build. Only Build moves.
runnerWait 4-9s and 'install dependencies' 1-2s on all 8, so neither runner queueing nor pnpm store coldness is involved.
e2eBuildCacheFinding.relationToPass1: Pass 1 measured gated 247s (<17Z) vs 357s (>=17Z) and e2e Build 50.5s vs 148s on a 34-run sample, and attributed it to hour-of-day cache churn. The hour correlation is probably real as a PROXY, but 11-16 shows the same 3.6x Build swing inside a 92-minute morning span, so the hour is not the mechanism. Cache restore hit/miss is. Treat pass 1's 'evening penalty' as 'runs that miss the fallback', which happens to be likelier late in the day.
e2eBuildCacheFinding.unproven: WHY some runs find a warm fallback and others do not. The cache key is runner.os-nextjs-e2e-<hash(pnpm-lock)>-<hash(web/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx})>, so it changes whenever any web source changes. A plausible mechanism is save latency vs merge-queue cadence: the entry is written at the END of the e2e job (~3-4 min in) while queue runs start 1-3 min apart, so a run often starts before the run that would populate its key has saved. NOT CONFIRMED — the toolset has no cache-API reader, and the 3 head SHAs of the fast runs (45a0789c59, 8e0140cd6a, 869714b4a9) landed after this checkout so their file lists are not inspectable locally.
e2eBuildCacheFinding.whyNoDiff: The fix lives in .github/workflows/pipeline.yml (cache key/path/save conditions, around lines 1417-1427), which this workflow is forbidden to edit even temporarily. Handed to a human as a report-only recommendation.

retriedTests.test: worker/src/__tests__/correctionScoreBilling.test.ts > counts CORRECTION score rows from the billing cutoff
retriedTests.status: CONFIRMED FLAKE — the reporter itself tagged it [flaky] on a run that SUCCEEDED, i.e. it failed twice then passed. This is the strong evidence standard, not an inference from retry count.
retriedTests.mechanism: The test writes 3 score rows that share the same id (one randomUUID reused) at cutoff+0ms/+1s/+2s and asserts all 3 are still counted. The scores table is ReplacingMergeTree(event_ts, is_deleted) ORDER BY (project_id, toDate(timestamp), name, id). CORRECTION_SCORES_BILLABLE_FROM is 2026-11-23T00:00:00.000Z, an exact UTC day boundary, so toDate(timestamp) is identical for all 3 rows. All 3 therefore share the COMPLETE sort key and are exact ReplacingMergeTree duplicates. Both getScoreCountsByProjectInCreationInterval and getScoreCountsByProjectAndDay are bare count(*) with no FINAL. Whether the assertions toBe(4)/toBe(3) hold depends on whether a background merge fires between the inserts and the SELECT, which is not deterministic.
retriedTests.productQuestion: The same non-determinism exists in the production billing queries, which are the same count(*)-without-FINAL. If repeated saves of one score id are meant to be billable, the count decays as merges run; if they are not, the pre-merge count over-counts. Flagged for a human — this run cannot see product intent.
